seoTitle: How to Find Google Workspace MX Records for Gmail
metaDescription: Learn how to find your Google Workspace MX records and add them to your domain's DNS settings to activate Gmail for your custom domain.
intro: Getting Gmail working with your own domain requires pointing your DNS to the correct MX records — without them, mail simply won't route through Google's servers. This guide shows where to find those records and how to add them correctly.

steps.heading: Open the Admin Console
steps.body: Sign in and navigate to the Gmail setup section, where Google displays the exact MX records needed for your domain.

steps.heading: Copy the MX record values
steps.body: Note the priority numbers and server addresses exactly as shown — these need to match precisely in your DNS settings.

steps.heading: Access your domain's DNS settings
steps.body: Log in to your domain provider (GoDaddy, Namecheap, Squarespace, or others) and locate the DNS management area.

steps.heading: Add the MX records to your DNS
steps.body: Enter each MX record with its correct priority value, replacing any existing conflicting records from your previous email provider.

steps.heading: Verify Gmail is working
steps.body: After DNS propagation, send a test email to your custom domain address to confirm it's arriving through Google Workspace correctly.

faq.question: Where exactly do I find my Google Workspace MX records?
faq.answer: They're listed in the Admin Console under the Gmail setup or domain settings section, ready to copy into your DNS provider.

faq.question: How many MX records does Google Workspace require?
faq.answer: Google typically provides a small set of MX records with different priority values that should all be added for reliable delivery.

faq.question: How long does it take for MX record changes to work?
faq.answer: DNS propagation can take anywhere from a few minutes to 48 hours depending on your domain provider and existing settings.

faq.question: What happens if I don't remove my old email provider's MX records?
faq.answer: Leaving old MX records in place can cause mail delivery conflicts, so it's important to remove them when adding Google's records.
